evidence.acsm_resistance_training_2026.k: Position stand overview of reviews for resistance-training prescription for muscle function, hypertrophy, and performance in healthy adults.
evidence.ashwell_wth_2016.key_finding: Supports waist-to-height ratio as a simple central-adiposity marker that can flag elevated risk earlier than BMI alone in the studied cohorts.
evidence.baevsky_hrv_method_2017.key_fin: Describes physiological rationale and computational methods for Baevsky-style heart-rate variability and stress-index measures.
evidence.brzycki_1rm_1993.key_finding: Describes the Brzycki formula estimating one-repetition maximum from repetitions to fatigue at a submaximal load.
evidence.buchheit_hrv_monitoring_2014.ke: Reviews practical HR/HRV monitoring, including smallest worthwhile change framing for interpreting day-to-day variation.
evidence.contreras_hip_thrust_emg_2015.k: In a small acute EMG study, the barbell hip thrust produced higher gluteus maximus activity than the back squat under the tested loads.
evidence.de_leva_segmental_1996.key_find: Provides adjusted segmental mass proportions used to estimate body-mass fractions supported in bodyweight exercises.
evidence.dickie_pullup_grip_emg_2017.key: EMG patterns across pull-up grip variations show grip-specific differences useful for coaching grip choice.
evidence.efsa_water_2010.key_finding: Sets adequate total water intakes for European age/sex groups from dietary reference value evidence.
evidence.epley_1rm_1985.key_finding: Presents the widely used Epley repetition-based estimate of one-repetition maximum from load and reps completed.
evidence.escamilla_squat_biomechanics_20: Reviews knee-joint loading and technique factors across squat styles relevant to safe coaching cues.
evidence.foster_srpe_2001.key_finding: Validates session-RPE × duration as a practical internal training-load metric across exercise modes.
evidence.garber_acsm_quantity_2011.key_f: ACSM guidance summarises dose ranges for cardiorespiratory, resistance, flexibility, and neuromotor exercise in apparently healthy adults.
evidence.gomez_ambrosi_cun_bae_2012.key_: Proposes the CUN-BAE equation estimating percent body fat from age, sex, and BMI, with clinic-population validation.
evidence.iom_water_2005.key_finding: Establishes Adequate Intake values for total water for the US/Canada DRI population by life stage and sex.
evidence.karvonen_hr_practical_1988.key_: Practical review of applying heart-rate methods, including reserve-based targets, during sports activities.
evidence.karvonen_hr_reserve_1957.key_fi: Classic source for prescribing intensity as a fraction of heart-rate reserve between resting and maximal heart rate.
evidence.mckenzie_dip_kinematics_2022.ke: Compares kinematics and muscle activity across bench, bar, and ring dips, informing progression and stability demands.
evidence.mckenzie_dip_shoulder_2020.key_: Discusses glenohumeral extension demands in the dip and coaching considerations that may reduce shoulder-injury risk.
evidence.mifflin_st_jeor_1990.key_findin: Derived sex-specific linear equations predicting resting energy expenditure from weight, height, and age in healthy adults.
evidence.morton_protein_2018.key_finding: Meta-regression supports diminishing returns for hypertrophy beyond roughly 1.6 g protein per kg body mass per day in healthy adults who lift.
evidence.munoz_polarized_runners_2014.ke: In recreational runners, a polarized intensity distribution improved performance markers relative to a between-thresholds emphasis in this trial.
evidence.nsca_essentials_4e.key_finding: Standard coaching reference for resistance-exercise technique, spotting, and programme design conventions used as technique/safety norms.
evidence.omnigart_mileage_caveat.key_fin: A fixed ~10% weekly mileage increase is a common coach heuristic without strong RCT support; readiness and injury signals should override it.
evidence.pelland_rt_dose_2025.key_findin: Meta-regressions relate weekly set volume and frequency to hypertrophy and strength, including fractional-set modelling of overlapping muscle work.
evidence.plews_hrv_adaptation_2013.key_f: Summarises how resting HRV trends can reflect training adaptation and overload risk when interpreted with context in elite endurance sport.
evidence.schoenfeld_frequency_2016.key_f: When weekly volume is not equated, training a muscle group at least twice weekly tends to favour hypertrophy versus once weekly.
evidence.schoenfeld_frequency_2019.key_f: With weekly volume equated, resistance-training frequency effects on hypertrophy are small to null in the pooled analyses.
evidence.schoenfeld_volume_2016.key_find: Meta-analysis reported greater hypertrophy with higher weekly set volumes, with diminishing returns at the upper end of studied ranges.
evidence.seiler_intensity_distribution_2: Describes a common ~80/20 easy-to-hard intensity distribution among endurance athletes as a training-organisation pattern, not a universal prescription.
evidence.suprak_pushup_load_2011.key_fin: Measured roughly 69–75% of body mass supported in traditional push-up positions, with lower fractions in modified variants.
evidence.tanaka_hrmax_2001.key_finding: Supports the 208 − 0.7×age prediction of maximal heart rate as an improvement over 220 − age in healthy adults.
evidence.who_bmi_2000.key_finding: Defines widely used adult BMI cut-points for underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obesity categories.
evidence.who_whr_2008.key_finding: Expert consultation report on measuring and interpreting waist circumference and waist–hip ratio for health risk screening.
evidence.youdas_pullup_chinup_emg_2010.k: Surface EMG differed by grip: chin-ups emphasised biceps and pectoralis more than pronated pull-ups in the tested sample.
evidence.al_haddad_hr_reliability_2011.k: Resting and post-exercise heart-rate and HRV-related measures show quantifiable reliability that informs day-to-day monitoring thresholds.
evidence.banister_trimp_1990.key_finding: Impulse–response (TRIMP-style) modelling relates training dose over time to performance fitness and fatigue components.
evidence.bellenger_hrv_status_2016.key_f: Pooled evidence links autonomic heart-rate regulation markers, including HRV, with changes in athletic training status.
evidence.hirshkowitz_sleep_duration_2015: Recommended sleep duration ranges by age band guide how much nightly sleep most healthy adults need.
evidence.impellizzeri_acwr_2021.key_find: The acute:chronic workload ratio rests on shaky causal assumptions; chronic load terms do not justify using ACWR as a universal injury predictor.
evidence.kaminsky_friend_vo2_2015.key_fi: Age- and sex-specific VO2 reference percentiles from the FRIEND registry provide norms for cardiorespiratory fitness interpretation.
evidence.loe_hunt_vo2_2016.key_finding: Population fitness models from HUNT support estimating VO2peak for wellness fitness comparisons when direct CPET is unavailable.
evidence.van_dongen_sleep_debt_2003.key_: Cumulative sleep restriction produces dose-dependent neurobehavioral deficits, supporting the concept of accumulating sleep debt.
evidence.watson_sleep_performance_2017.k: Insufficient sleep impairs athletic performance, cognition and injury risk markers; extending sleep and protecting sleep opportunity support recovery.
claim.formula_ree_mifflin_st_jeor.text: Resting energy expenditure is estimated with the Mifflin–St Jeor equations from weight, height, age and sex.
claim.formula_hrmax_tanaka.text: Age-predicted maximal heart rate uses Tanaka’s 208 − 0.7×age equation rather than 220 − age.
claim.formula_hr_zone_karvonen.text: Heart-rate training zones can be set from a fraction of heart-rate reserve (Karvonen method).
claim.formula_hrmax_gellish.text: An alternative age-predicted HRmax is about 207 − 0.7×age (Gellish longitudinal model).
claim.formula_hrmax_nes.text: An alternative age-predicted HRmax from the HUNT Fitness Study is 211 − 0.64×age (Nes).
claim.formula_hrmax_gulati_women.text: Women’s chronotropic expectations and risk markers from large exercise-test cohorts inform sex-aware HR interpretation (Gulati).
claim.formula_bodyfat_cun_bae.text: Percent body fat can be estimated with the CUN-BAE equation from age, sex and BMI.
claim.formula_bodyfat_deurenberg.text: Percent body fat can be estimated from BMI using Deurenberg age- and sex-specific formulas.
claim.formula_bodyfat_rfm.text: Relative fat mass (RFM) estimates body-fat percentage from height and waist circumference.
claim.prog_weekly_set_volume_hypertrophy: Weekly hard-set volume for a muscle relates to hypertrophy in a graded way, with diminishing returns at high volumes.
claim.prog_muscle_frequency_twice_weekly: Training each major muscle at least twice weekly tends to favour hypertrophy when weekly volume is not equated.
claim.prog_frequency_volume_equated.text: When weekly volume is equated, training frequency has small effects on hypertrophy and mainly helps distribute sets.
claim.prog_acsm_rt_prescription.text: Resistance-training prescription for healthy adults follows ACSM review-level guidance for strength and hypertrophy.
claim.prog_acsm_quantity_quality.text: Weekly exercise quantity and quality targets follow ACSM guidance for cardiorespiratory, musculoskeletal and neuromotor fitness.
Higher total daily protein, around up to ~1.6 g·kg⁻¹·day⁻¹, modestly augments resistance-training gains in healthy adults.
claim.nutrition_protein_older_adults.tex: Protein supplementation effects in nonfrail older adults are modest and depend on baseline intake and training.
claim.nutrition_water_adequate_intake.te: Adequate total water intake is about 2.5 L/day for men and 2.0 L/day for women from all sources, higher with heat or hard training.
claim.recovery_sleep_performance.text: Enough sleep supports athletic performance, cognition and recovery; short sleep impairs them.
claim.recovery_hrv_guided_training.text: Trends in resting heart-rate variability can help decide when to push or hold hard endurance sessions.
claim.recovery_baevsky_stress_index.text: A Baevsky-style stress index from RR-interval statistics is one optional HRV tension marker, interpreted cautiously.
claim.recovery_pss10_stress.text: Perceived stress can be tracked with the validated 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10).
claim.load_session_rpe.text: Internal training load can be scored as session-RPE × session duration (Foster).
claim.load_trimp.text: Training impulses (TRIMP) model how training dose accumulates into fitness and fatigue over time.
claim.load_acwr_caution.text: The acute:chronic workload ratio should not be treated as a universal injury crystal ball.
claim.cardio_polarized_distribution.text: Endurance progress often emphasises mostly easy volume with a smaller share of high-intensity work (polarised distribution).
claim.cardio_mileage_10pct_caveat.text: A fixed ~10% weekly mileage cap is only a soft heuristic; readiness and pain signals matter more.
claim.exercise_technique_safety.text: Exercise technique and spotting standards follow established strength-conditioning coaching references.
claim.exercise_programming_volume.text: Programme templates place weekly set targets in ranges supported by hypertrophy dose–response evidence.
claim.exercise_mobility_flexibility.text: Flexibility and neuromotor work are included per ACSM quantity/quality guidance for healthy adults.
claim.squat_knee_biomechanics.text: Squat depth and technique are coached with reference to published knee-biomechanics analyses.
claim.hip_thrust_glute_emg.text: Hip-thrust variations are offered for glute-focused work based on comparative EMG evidence.
claim.segment_inertia_load_model.text: Body-segment mass estimates for load models use adjusted anthropometric inertia parameters.
claim.pullup_variation_emg.text: Pull-up grip and technique variations change measured upper-body muscle activation.
claim.pullup_chinup_emg.text: Pull-up and chin-up variants differ in surface EMG and elbow motion patterns.
claim.dip_shoulder_extension_safety.text: Dip depth and shoulder extension are coached with caution for glenohumeral stress.
claim.dip_apparatus_kinematics.text: Bench, bar and ring dips differ in kinematics and muscle activity.
claim.bodyweight_support_fraction.text: Closed-chain push-up-family positions change the percentage of body mass supported.
claim.insight_daily_readiness.text: Daily readiness is a wellness estimate from ln rMSSD versus personal baselines, resting heart rate, and recent sleep — not a medical diagnosis.
claim.insight_load_target.text: Load targets use session-RPE acute and chronic averages as a soft daily range guide, with known limits of acute:chronic ratios.
claim.insight_sleep_balance_need.text: Sleep need for healthy adults is guided by consensus duration ranges, then personalised when the user sets a preferred target.
claim.insight_sleep_balance_debt.text: Sleep debt accumulates when recent sleep falls short of need; it is a wellness balance estimate, not a clinical disorder score.
claim.insight_habit_effect_caveats.text: Habit-note effect contrasts are simple within-person paired comparisons and stay low-confidence when samples are small or noisy.
claim.insight_out_of_range_baseline.text: Out-of-range notes flag metrics that deviate from a personal rolling baseline, for awareness rather than diagnosis.
claim.insight_weekly_overview.text: Weekly overview aggregates readiness, load, and sleep wellness estimates to summarise the past week.
claim.insight_day_reserve.text: Day reserve estimates remaining training headroom from readiness and load context as a wellness guide only.
claim.insight_fitness_age_vo2_norms.text: Fitness age maps estimated VO2max onto age- and sex-specific cardiorespiratory fitness norms as a wellness comparison.
